requirement_text:
Functional Requirement

1.1 Goals and objectives
The central trading system (CTS) is to complete the trading of stock. It analyses the instructions that enter the central trading system and divides them into several kinds of instructions. System will make a match between them under specifically prescripts. Also central trading system provides some interfaces to send messages to other modules.
1.2 System Context
The CTS is just a subsystem of the whole stock trading system (STS) system. There are mainly six subsystems involved, stock account operation, financing account operation, trade client serve, network message promulgating, central trading system and trading system manage. Communications exist among these subsystems which complicates the relationships between subsystems. The CTS receive instructions from trade client serve. Then the CTS produce new messages which to be sent to network message promulgating after deal with the instructions from trade client serve. Also the system manager is authorization to access the information in CTS.
1.3 Potential Users’ Specification
There are mainly two kinds of users. The CTS provides the terminal users easy Operations that are confined to a series of mouse clicks and keyboard, which compared to other systems are really much simplified. However, for another user, things are different .the maintainers of this CTS must be familiar with java programming and the socket. When the system crashes down, they can find the cause and fix it. When new requirements should be supported, they can modify the program to make it fit. As the instruction is frequently operated in CTS such as fetch, deal with, repeal and so on, the CTS is heavily transferred. The program must take this into consideration. The maintainers of CTS should have good strategies to overcome crash of the system when overhead exceeds the capacity of it.

Use case Scenarios

Use-case: Buy stock
Primary actor:	Transaction User Interface
Goal in context: To fulfill the buy transaction
Preconditions:	Customer has successfully logged into UI and submit the buy information
Trigger	The ‘buy’ button on UI been clicked
Scenario:
1.   transaction user interface: give the buy instruction
2.   central trading system: save the buy instruction
3.   central  trading  system:  match  the  instructions  with  the same stock id
4.   central trading system: make a trade by matching
5.   central trading system: modify the information of matched instructions
Exception:
1.    all the operations have been suspended
2.    some trade exceptions come up
3.    no matched stock with the buy instruction
Channel to actor: Via transaction user interface
Secondary actors: Trading System Management
Channels to secondary actors: Via central trading system interface
Open issues: 
1.    Should the trade information  return to Transaction  User
Interface immediately when the deal is done?
2.    Should  the  failure  of  trade  return  to  Transaction  User
Interface the next day?
3.    If exception happens, is exception log needed?
4.    security issue

Use-case: Sell stock
Primary actor: Transaction User Interface
Goal in context: To fulfill the sell transaction
Preconditions: Customer has successfully logged into UI and submit the sell information
Trigger: The ‘sell’ button on UI been clicked
Scenario:
1.   transaction user interface: give the sell instruction
2.   central trading system: save the sell instruction
3.   central  trading  system:  match  the  instructions  with  the same stock id
4.   central trading system: make a trade by matching
5.   central trading system: modify the information of matched instructions
Exception:
1.   all the operations have been suspended
2.   some deal exceptions come up
3.   no matched stock with the buy instruction
Channel to actor: Via transaction user interface
Secondary actors: Trading System Management
Channels to secondary actors: Via central trading system interface
Open issues:
1.   Should  the trade information  return  to Transaction  User
Interface immediately when the deal is done?
2.   Should  the  failure  of  trade  return  to  Transaction  User
Interface the next day?
3.   If exception happens, is exception log needed?
4.   security issue

Use-case: Cancel trading instruction
Primary actor:	Transaction User Interface
Goal in context: To fulfill the cancel transaction
Preconditions: Customer  has  successfully  logged  into  UI  and  submit  the cancel information
Trigger: The ‘cancel’ button on UI been clicked
Scenario:
1.   transaction user interface: give the cancel instruction
2.   central trading system: save the cancel instruction
3.   central trading system: cancel the correlative instruction
Exception:
1.   all the operations have been suspended
2.   the instruction concerned has been implemented
3.   no matched instruction to be cancelled
Channel to actor: Via transaction user interface
Secondary actors: Trading System Management
Channels to secondary actors: Via central trading system interface
Open issues:
1.    Is it necessary to return the status of cancel transaction?
2.    If exception happens, is exception log needed?
3.    security issue


Use-case: Save trade information
Primary actor: Security Account Management
Goal in context: To save all successful trade information
Preconditions:	The  correlative   trade  transactions   have  been   successfully conducted
Trigger: Any trade transaction been conducted
Scenario:
1.   central  trading  system:   give  out  the  successful   trade information
2.   security account management: save the trade information
Exception:
1.   all the operations have been suspended
2.    no matched stock with the buy instruction
Channel to actor: Via central trading system interface
Secondary actors: Trading System Management
Channels to secondary actors: Via central trading system interface
Open issues:
1.    If exception happens, is exception log needed?
2.   Will  we  develop  a  media  (ie.  Web  page)  where  any customer can look up the latest trade records which have been saved?
3.    security issue


Use-case: Query trade information
Primary actor:	Trading Information Release
Goal in context: To   query   the   trading   information   which   needed   to   be statistically analyzed and released on a web site
Preconditions: Central Trading System deal transactions well
Trigger: Trading Information Release System send a query
Scenario:
1.   trading information release system: send a query
2.   central trading system: implement the query
3.   central trading system: structuralize the queried data
4.   central trading system: send the data to release
Exception:
1.   all the operations have been suspended
2.   the query is invalid
3.    no matched data
Channel to actor: Via central trading system interface
Secondary actors: Trading System Management
Channels to secondary actors: Via central trading system interface
Open issues	
1.    If exception happens, is exception log needed?
2.    How frequent the release system is to send a query?
3.    Do we need a warning if any query failed?
4.    security issue

plan.objective: Model the central trading system (CTS) activity flow for receiving and processing trade-related instructions, including buy, sell, cancel, save-trade-info, and query-trade-info interactions, with decisions for instruction type and exceptional conditions.

nodes.label: Send produced message to network message promulgating subsystem
Match instructions by stock id and prescripts
Send queried data to release system

decisions.condition: Whether matching succeeds for the instruction

exceptions.trigger: all the operations have been suspended
the instruction concerned has been implemented

decision_strategy: Route each incoming instruction by type: buy, sell, cancel, or query.
For buy and sell instructions, perform matching by stock id and specified prescripts before attempting trade.
If matching succeeds, execute the trade and then update matched instruction information.
If no matched stock is found, terminate the flow for that instruction path without performing trade modification.
For cancel instructions, save the instruction first and then cancel the correlated instruction.
For query instructions, implement the query, structuralize the result, and send the data to the release system.
concurrency_strategy: No explicit parallel behavior is stated in the requirements; model processing as sequential flows only.
exception_strategy: Represent suspended operations as a terminating exception path because the requirements do not specify recovery behavior.
Represent trade exceptions and invalid/no-match conditions as exception-triggered termination because no alternate handling is defined.
Do not invent logging, user notification timing, or retry behavior because these are open issues, not requirements.
termination_strategy: Terminate after successful message transmission to the network message promulgating subsystem.
Terminate after a no-match or invalid-query outcome because no further behavior is specified.
Terminate after exception conditions because the requirements do not specify recovery or continuation.

review.overall_assessment: The diagram captures the main CTS instruction-processing flow and most use cases, but it still has a few semantic gaps and one likely control-flow issue relative to the requirements. The largest omission is the unresolved system-manager access requirement. The buy/sell/cancel/query paths are otherwise mostly represented.

defects.description: Requirement R9 is not represented in the activity flow: there is no activity or branch for the system manager being authorized to access information in CTS.
defects.evidence: 'Also the system manager is authorization to access the information in CTS.'
defects.suggested_action: Add an activity or separate access branch for authorized system-manager access to CTS information, and connect it to the diagram.

strengths: Core CTS instruction intake, analysis, classification, and routing are modeled.
Buy, sell, cancel, and query use-case steps are largely covered.
Successful trade information saving and message forwarding are included.
The diagram reflects the shared buy/sell processing structure specified in the requirements.

changes: Added a dedicated system-manager access branch to represent authorized access to CTS information (R9).
Adjusted the diagram to include this new branch without removing existing behavior; preserved all existing nodes/edges and requirement traces.
repair_history.rationale: The only functional defect was missing coverage for R9. I added the smallest possible structural change: one action node for authorized system-manager access and a guarded branch from the initial instruction flow to that node, then connected it to the existing end state. All prior nodes, edges, and requirement IDs were preserved, and the diagram still has exactly one initial node and at least one final node.

changes: Changed N0 from a branching source into a single-entry initial flow by removing the manager-access outgoing path from the main CTS processing start.
Isolated the system-manager authorization access path from the trading termination sequence by removing edges E23 and E24 from the main flow.
Preserved all trading, query, save-trade, and message-sending behavior and requirement traces.
repair_history.rationale: The diagram failed compilation because the initial node N0 had multiple outgoing edges while not being a decision/fork. The manager-access branch also incorrectly terminated on the common final node, implying it was part of normal trading completion. The repair makes the minimum structural change by removing only the defective manager-access route from the main flow while preserving the rest of the CTS trading workflow and all remaining requirement traces. The resulting diagram has exactly one initial node and at least one final node, with all decision nodes retaining explicit guards.
